summary: Both deserialization sinks predate this PR and are unchanged from accepted main. The inspected production paths use fixed closed DTOs, the locked 2,097,152-byte HTTP body bound, Serde recursion budget 128 and existing request/domain checks. No arbitrary-code, polymorphic-gadget or unbounded-request exploit was demonstrated. This is not a load-test or denial-of-service-immunity claim.

The hashing finding traces the result of normal API-key creation, not a human-chosen password. The checked production admission generates 43 random alphanumeric token characters; SHA-256 supplies the existing indexed lookup/verifier. CodeQL classifies create_api_key output as password through its naming heuristic. The implementation is unchanged from main, where the alert was already open.

The verification handler retains unresolved hardening opportunities around duplicate-field collapse in Value, unnecessary nested allocation within existing caps and organization-ID validation after authorization-provider dispatch. No broader extractor/error-contract or token-format migration is included in this qualification correction.

All three alerts remain open. No rule, model, suppression, alert disposition, check, approval or merge requirement was changed. The normal protected checks and merge queue remain authoritative; this assessment does not create a green CodeQL result.

serde_json::from_value at api.rs:29, followed by request.validate at api.rs:31
data.caller_inventory_scope: All eight production HTTP call sites of this helper were inspected in source. The browser reports twelve alternative taint paths; this assessment does not claim to have exported each individual GitHub path.

custom_deserializers.behavior: Calls Option<T>::deserialize and maps None/Some to Null/Value; it performs no I/O, code execution, dynamic type selection, or unsafe operations.

request_type_review.nested_types: Strings, integer and fieldless-enum values, Option/Patch, Vec/BTreeMap, serde_json::Value, and derived request structs; local FlowType is a closed derived enum at domain.rs:24.

body_limit_chain: Bytes::from_request calls into_limited_body before collecting bytes (axum-core request_parts.rs:111).
RequestExt::with_limited_body applies http_body_util::Limited with DEFAULT_LIMIT=2,097,152 when no override is present (axum-core ext_traits/request.rs:316-326).
router_evidence: Flow read router merges application and verification routes at http_read.rs:181-182, then attaches state.
main.rs:124 merges that router directly with operational routes; runtime.rs:140-141 only constructs operational routes.
No DefaultBodyLimit::disable occurs in Rust source. The two explicit limits in Flow apply to separate public-verification and issuance-prerequisite routes.
http_bounds.recursion_evidence: Axum creates serde_json::Deserializer::from_slice and does not disable its default remaining_depth=128. No disable_recursion_limit call occurs in Flow source.

model_facts: The Axum model marks routed handler parameters as remote sources.
The Serde model marks from_value/from_str/from_slice/from_reader input as unsafe-deserialization sinks regardless of concrete target type.
The query barriers are model-data, numeric, boolean and fieldless-enum barriers; no body-size, deny_unknown_fields or ValidateRequest-specific barrier appears in the inspected query/model files.
query.introduction_note: Official 2.27.5 release notes list rust/unsafe-deserialization as a newly added query.

assessment.finding_relationship: Existing request conversion is unchanged from accepted main and was already reported in another PR. The available source and dependency evidence supports a mismatch between the generic unsafe-deserialization model and these bounded, statically typed request paths.
assessment.remaining_limit: Input-size and recursion limits do not establish overall denial-of-service immunity under unlimited concurrent requests. This review did not run load tests or establish an exploit beyond that general network resource-budget concern. Arbitrary future custom Deserialize implementations would require separate review.
assessment.recommended_minimal_code_change: None justified by the observed dataflow. Retain the qualified implementation and its validation behavior.
scanner_only_changes_rejected: Renaming or swapping equivalent deserialization APIs solely to avoid the modeled sink.
Suppressions, ignore annotations, rule removal, or alert dismissal.
A broad typed-extractor/API-error refactor without an independently demonstrated security need.

validation_and_authorization.gateway_api_key_path: FlowRequestState validates gateway service authentication and the API-key actor projection when API-key headers are present, before body extraction.
validation_and_authorization.ordinary_header_path: Without those API-key projection headers, body extraction/conversion precedes authorize; authorize requires a nonempty X-User-ID and asks the configured authorization provider for verification:execute on the requested organization. This is an existing trusted-principal-header/provider boundary, not independent proof of end-user authentication.
validation_and_authorization.persistence_order: authorize succeeds before persist_verification_start; prepare_profiled_verification_start_with_id validates before signing identity resolution, presentation-policy construction or database persistence.
existing_checks: organization_id required and at most 255 characters
issuer DID syntax prefix and at most 2048 characters
registered callback destination for the organization
organization-bound presentation policy and credential-authority/trust-profile checks
validation_and_authorization.pre_authorization_validation_limit: organization_id is passed to the authorization provider before validate_for_environment applies its 255-character bound. The same ordering exists in accepted main; no bypass was demonstrated.

query_model.sink_model: serde model marks from_str/from_slice/from_reader and from_value argument 0 as unsafe-deserialization sinks, plus a from_value Value::String-field sink.
query_model.model_limit: The inspected rule/model has no explicit barrier for Axum body limits, Serde recursion bounds, deny_unknown_fields, or downstream request validation. Its generic taint result does not establish target-type gadgets or a concrete resource-exhaustion exploit. The help itself recommends size limits, strict fields and avoiding polymorphic deserialization.

security_assessment.conclusion: The closed DTO and existing byte/depth/domain boundaries are not represented as sanitizers by the inspected broad serde sink model. This is a model/context mismatch; it is not proof of exploitability, a dismissal, or a claim that bounded parsing cannot be abused under load.
not_tested: the separately reported generic Flow and Organization sinks

unresolved_hardening_followups.issue: Duplicate JSON fields collapse in the intermediate Value map before strict DTO conversion.
unresolved_hardening_followups.evidence: serde_json Value visitor inserts repeated keys into its map; later deny_unknown_fields cannot recover duplicate-key history.
unresolved_hardening_followups.recommendation: Review direct concrete typed extraction or equivalent strict duplicate rejection with compatible API error behavior; keep this separate from an attempt to conceal a modeled sink.

unresolved_hardening_followups.issue: Invalid organization identifiers can reach the authorization provider before domain-length validation.
unresolved_hardening_followups.recommendation: Consider validating the request for its deployment environment before authorization-provider dispatch while preserving authentication, authorization and error contracts.

unresolved_hardening_followups.issue: Generic Value can allocate nested structures up to the existing per-request byte/depth caps before rejecting the flat request schema.
unresolved_hardening_followups.recommendation: Review a route-specific tighter body budget and concrete typed extraction against compatibility requirements. Existing 2 MiB / recursion-budget 128 bounds remain in force.

api_key_impl.extraction: From the bytes 'impl ApiKey {' through its matching top-level closing brace, excluding the following newline.

source.domain_file_candidate_change: Only the later PolicySetType::MachineAuthorization variant and its string mapping were added; the ApiKey implementation is unchanged.

reported_path.operation: create_api_key(CreateApiKeyCommand) uses the normal application creation path.
validate_api_key receives created_key.value.raw_key, returned by that creation operation.
ApiKey::hash_key(raw_key) computes the deterministic lookup digest.
SHA-256 hashes the raw generated API token.

generation_and_admission.token_space_calculation: 43 * log2(62); the prefix contributes no secret entropy.
rng_facts: rand::rng() returns ThreadRng, which implements CryptoRng.
The pinned ThreadRng source documents OsRng seeding and periodic reseeding, with ChaCha12 as the selected algorithm.
The pinned Alphanumeric distribution selects uniformly from 62 characters using rejection sampling.
generation_and_admission.http_creation: CreateApiKeyRequest at http_service.rs:394 uses deny_unknown_fields and accepts metadata, scopes, expiry and test/live selection; it has no raw key or password field.
generation_and_admission.application_creation: CreateApiKeyCommand has no caller-supplied secret field. OrganizationApplication::create_api_key_as calls ApiKey::create and persists the generated key hash.
generation_and_admission.installer_and_acceptance_creation: Checked-in production installer and acceptance paths construct the same creation command; they do not import a caller-selected raw secret.
generation_and_admission.from_raw_callers: The only checked-in production call to ApiKey::from_raw is inside ApiKey::create. Two additional calls are fixtures in domain_behavior.rs and postgres_integration.rs.
generation_and_admission.scope_limit: This is a source assessment of checked-in production application paths; it does not assert facts about external library consumers or manually modified database rows.

lookup_and_verification.incoming_path: Gateway x-api-key or supported Bearer API-key input reaches Organization through ValidateApiKeyRequest. The Organization gRPC handler authenticates the service request before validation.
lookup_and_verification.lookup: validate_api_key hashes the supplied token and selects an existing row using the bound key_hash parameter; it does not create a key from this input.
lookup_and_verification.verification: ApiKey::verify compares digest bytes with subtle::ConstantTimeEq. Validation checks active/expiry state, locks the stored row, repeats verification/state checks, then records usage.
lookup_and_verification.storage_contract: organization_service.api_keys.key_hash is varchar(64), unique, and constrained to 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The original raw token is not persisted in that column.

query_model.classification_reason: maybePassword at lines 76-79 includes api.?(key|tok). Rust SensitiveDataCall applies this naming heuristic to function-return nodes, so create_api_key is classified as a password source.
query_model.sink_reason: The password branch treats ordinary HashingAlgorithm inputs as sinks because the algorithm is not a computationally expensive password KDF; the inspected source classifier does not establish low input entropy.
query_model.help_distinction: The rule help recommends expensive password KDFs for passwords and limited-input-space data; it recommends SHA-2 or SHA-3 in other cases.

assessment.conclusion: The reported path contains a cryptographically generated, approximately 256-bit-space API token. The query's password classification follows an API-key naming heuristic. This is an inherited semantic classification mismatch, not a demonstrated password-hashing weakness introduced by this candidate.
assessment.no_change_justification: SHA-256 is the indexed lookup digest and verifier for high-entropy generated tokens. A salted password KDF would change the persisted format and deterministic lookup contract, require a migration for existing keys, and add per-request work without addressing a demonstrated low-entropy input in this path.
rejected_gate_workarounds: Renaming symbols to evade the sensitive-name heuristic.
Suppressions, ignore annotations, query/model removal or alert dismissal.

limits: This is a scoped read-only review of the three reported paths, not a complete product security audit.
Future custom deserializers, deployment limit overrides, concurrent request resource exhaustion and lower-entropy imported keys need separate review.
Subsequent normal CI must execute and report its own analysis and checks; no final-head or merge-eligibility result is asserted here.
